The main takeaway from our work is that
Early Permian sedimentary rocks of the northern Perth Basin were sourced by a mixture of cratonic and orogenic terranes, which were dispersed within the basin by a variety of processes.

, despite being a relatively short-lived basin, the northeastern Perth Basin was fed by a diverse set of sediment sources, including both cratonic and orogenic terranes, which are not easily recognized in a single provenance study.

a combination of sedimentary and provenance data provides the best constraints to reconstruct paleogeography of sedimentary basins and to understand the evolution of sedimentary systems in space and time.
